Question: australian immigration news

Answer: Recent Australian immigration news includes updates on migration program planning, visa application charge adjustments, and news related to specific visa types and processing times. The government is shifting to a multi-year planning model for migration, extending the outlook to four years from the current one-year cycle, starting in 2025-26. Additionally, visa application charges will increase by 3% from July 1, 2025, with a targeted increase for student visas.
This video discusses changes to PTE scores for skilled migration and updates on skilled visa income thresholds for 2025:
Key Updates and News::
- Multi-Year Planning: The Migration Program will adopt a four-year planning horizon, with public consultation on the first cycle (2025-26 to 2028-29) commencing later this year.
- Visa Application Charges: Most visa application charges will increase by 3% from July 1, 2025, and there will be a targeted increase for student and student guardian visas.
- Skilled Visa Income Thresholds: Skilled visa income thresholds will increase by 4.6% from July 1, 2025.
- Northern Territory DAMA: A new Designated Area Migration Agreement (DAMA) for the Northern Territory will be effective from March 2025 to June 30, 2030.
- Processing Times: Visa processing times are improving across most visa programs, particularly temporary visas, with older applications being prioritized.
- Migration Agent Sanctions: Two migration agents were sanctioned in May 2025 for breaching their obligations under the Code of Conduct.
- Pacific Engagement Visa (PEV): People selected in the January and February PEV ballots need to lodge their visa applications soon.
- Parent Visa Updates: New online services have been introduced to support paper-based parent visa applications.
- Core Skills Occupation List: The Core Skills Occupation List (CSOL) was released on December 3, 2024, replacing complex occupation lists.
- Visa Scams: The Department of Home Affairs is reminding applicants to be aware of visa scams.
